lesson_body:
Welcome to our first day of mathematics learning in Grade Kindergarten! Today, we will embark on an exciting journey called 'Unit 1 Foundations'. The focus of our lesson is to introduce the fundamental concepts of numbers and counting. We will learn how to recognize numbers from 1 to 10 and understand the important place they hold in our world.

To start our day, let’s gather in a circle. We will sing the 'Five Little Ducks' song to warm up our voices and minds. This song will help us count down as we say goodbye to the little ducks and practice recognizing the numbers. After our song, I will show you a bright and colorful number chart from 1 to 10. We will point to each number together, clapping as we say them out loud. This will reinforce our number recognition and build excitement about learning about numbers.

Next, we’ll read a picture book called 'Ten Black Dots' by Donald Crews. This story uses dots to illustrate how numbers can represent quantities. As we read, I will ask questions about how many dots we see on each page, encouraging you to count aloud with me. We will also talk about what we can make with dots, such as shapes or pictures, fostering both creativity and math skills simultaneously.

After the story, we'll transition into building our own dot art. Each child will receive a worksheet with a dotted outline of various objects. Using crayons, markers, or dot stickers, you will fill in the outlines and decorate them. As you work, I will circulate through the room, prompting you to count the dots as you go. This activity encourages both counting practice and fine motor skills development. Finally, we will conclude our lesson by sharing our artwork with the class, allowing you to practice describing your creations and reinforcing your counting skills in a fun and engaging way.
interactive_assignment: For our hands-on activity, we will create a 'Number Wall'. Each child will receive a piece of construction paper and a specific number from 1 to 10. Your task is to decorate your paper with that number using materials from our craft supply box—think stickers, crayons, or even cut-out shapes! Once you have created your number, we will hang them up on our classroom wall. This way, we will have a vibrant and interactive display of numbers. As part of your assignment, I would like you to also draw a simple representation of the quantity that corresponds to your number, such as 3 apples for the number 3. This creative activity will allow you to physically engage with numbers and see their value visually.

daily_assessment.prompt:
How many apples are there if you have drawn three apples on your paper? Please choose the correct answer:
1. Two apples
2. Three apples
3. Five apples
4. One apple
